issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses permit X={0}. Taking the identity matrix gives operator norm zero on H_{X,σ}, whereas the scalar embedding has norm σ_1^{-1}>0. The reverse inequality assumes the existence of a unit vector η_1, which does not exist in this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume X is nonzero in the equality and lower-bound statements, and handle X={0} separately with zero errors and widths.
issues.overall_effect: The norm and sampling-width equalities, and the positive quasi-optimality lower bound, fail for the zero Hilbert space. The upper error bounds remain valid there.
issues.title: The operator-norm equality requires a nonzero target Hilbert space
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate-case correction requiring no change to the method or convergence rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and $V_m = \operatorname{span}\{\varphi_s\}_{s=1}^{m}$ the subspace spanned by the functions $\varphi_s$ corresponding to the $m$ smallest $\sigma_s$.

issues.failure_explanation: Every stated least-squares output lies in V_m, so its unit-ball worst-case error is at least d_m, by testing σ_{m+1}^{-1}φ_{m+1}. Take σ_s=2^s. For parts (ii) and (iii), m=n and ∑_{s≥n}d_s²=(4/3)d_n². Their right-hand sides are therefore respectively d_n√(4 log n/(3n)) and d_n√(4/(3n)), both smaller than d_n for n≥90. Part (i) also fails because its tail begins near 20m rather than near the actual truncation dimension. These scalar estimates cannot hold for the prescribed algorithms, regardless of the sample points or probability.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply dimension-consistent scalar estimates that include the truncation term d_m and appropriately indexed tails, or enlarge the approximation spaces relative to the tail thresholds and adjust the constant sampling budgets. Then repeat the transfer and rate calculation; the established bound d_m≲N m^{-1/q} permits the advertised polynomial rates to survive.
issues.overall_effect: All three foundational least-squares inequalities are false as stated, leaving the subsequent rate proofs without their asserted scalar input.
issues.title: The tail bounds contradict the unavoidable truncation error of V_m
issues.why_classification: A corrected scalar approximation lemma or a contained reconstruction reparameterization is necessary. This is more than a constant correction, but it need not change the Bochner reduction or the advertised ℓq convergence exponents.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Denote by $\Ss_n^X$  the family of all linear sampling algorithms $S_k^X$ in $L_2(U,X;\mu)$ of the form \eqref{S_k} with $k \le n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition gives ρ_{c3 n}≤error(S_{c3 n}), not the displayed comparison for ρ_n. There is no general constant-factor comparison of these errors under arbitrary admissible spectra. For example, an (n+1)-atom block with an n-dimensional zero-mean head and a small constant mode of size ε has an n-sample obstruction of order ε√n, while oversampled least squares onto the head has error O(ε). An arbitrarily small infinite tail can be appended to fit the stated setting.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the direct comparison by ρ_{c3 n}≤error(S_{c3 n}), then apply the error estimate at floor(n/c3) to obtain the claimed n-sampling-width rate, treating the remaining small n separately.
issues.overall_effect: The first inequality in the displayed chains is unsupported and generally false, although the final polynomial sampling-width rate can still be obtained by reindexing.
issues.title: An n-sampling width is compared directly with a c3 n-sample algorithm
issues.why_classification: A routine sample-budget reindexing preserves the final convergence rate and the actual algorithmic error guarantees.

issues.overall_effect: The proof's normalization of the M,N dependence is invalid, and the subsequent rate applications inherit that proof gap.
issues.title: The normalization incorrectly treats N as a radius of a fixed weighted ball
issues.why_classification: The source already supplies the homogeneity and width estimate needed for a short local repair preserving every rate and constant dependence.

Hence ∑_k σ_{k e_j}^{-q} diverges whenever ηq≤2. For instance, q=1, η=1, ρ_j=2^j and ψ_j=0 satisfy every stated input condition, but the asserted reciprocal ℓ1 summability is false.

issues.failure_explanation: Positive radii smaller than one do not let the weighted smallness condition control a(y) on [-1,1]^∞. Take spatially constant ā=1, ψ_1=2, ρ_1=1/4, ψ_j=0 and ρ_j=2^j for j≥2. The weighted ratio is 1/2 and the reciprocal radii belong to every ℓq, but a(y)=1+2y_1 vanishes at y_1=-1/2. For nonzero f the solution is u_0/(1+2y_1), which is not L2 under any of the stated Jacobi measures because their densities are positive at that interior point.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require ρ_j>1 for every j, so the stated weighted smallness condition implies uniform ellipticity on the parameter cube; use these radii in the coefficient-weight result.
issues.overall_effect: The affine lemma admits inputs for which the claimed L2 solution and weighted coefficient estimate do not exist.
issues.title: The affine hypotheses do not ensure ellipticity
issues.why_classification: A standard missing lower-bound hypothesis restores the ellipticity required by the model without changing the sampling method, q-range, or convergence rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The source defines the Jacobi measure's scalar normalizer c_{a,b}, but nowhere defines the sequence c_k^{a,b} used here or relates it to J_k. Its values and growth determine both claimed summability properties. Even the infinite product over zero coordinates requires c_0^{a,b}=1, which is not specified. Thus this is not a usable definition of σ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a fully specified Jacobi-weight lemma defining all c_k^{a,b}, including c_0^{a,b}=1, and establishing both the weighted coefficient bound and reciprocal summability for that definition. Then use that sequence in the affine sampling construction.
issues.overall_effect: The affine weight sequence, its reciprocal norm, and the sampling densities and approximation spaces depending on it are unspecified.
issues.title: The affine Jacobi weights contain an undefined sequence
issues.why_classification: A contained coefficient-weight lemma and explicit normalization are missing, rather than merely an algebraic step. They can be supplied within the existing approximation architecture.
